findings.highlight: I've only heard the gist of it from Takeya… so you were the one plotting things behind the scenes.
findings.evidenceJa:
武也たちから肝心なことだけは聞かされてないんだな…
首謀者なのに浮かばれない奴。
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that Takeya has not told Koharu the one crucial fact and pities the unrewarded mastermind; the English says Haruki heard only the gist and identifies Koharu as the plotter.
findings.japanese:
武也たちから肝心なことだけは聞かされてないんだな…
首謀者なのに浮かばれない奴。
findings.todokanai: I've only heard the gist of it from Takeya… so you were the one plotting things behind the scenes.

findings.highlight: "He must've been thinking about his girlfriend…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「彼女と一悶着あったと考えるのが…」
findings.explanation: The coworkers conclude it is reasonable to infer that Haruki had trouble or a quarrel with his girlfriend; the English says he must have been thinking about her.
findings.japanese: 「彼女と一悶着あったと考えるのが…」
findings.todokanai: "He must've been thinking about his girlfriend…"

findings.evidenceJa: けど、少しだ。あの頃に比べれば全然余裕で日々を普通に過ごしてる。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his present depression is only slight; compared with his earlier collapse, he now has ample emotional room to live normally. The English attaches 'only a little' to his recovery and says he is only slightly better, reversing the degree of improvement he is trying to reassure Mari about.
findings.japanese:
けど、少しだ。
あの頃に比べれば全然余裕で日々を普通に過ごしてる。
findings.todokanai: Though only a little better. Compared to that time, I'm living out my days quite normally.

findings.highlight: if you look at it from a different angle, it doesn't seem like there's any issue
findings.evidenceJa: あいつに甘やかされすぎてそうなってしまった側面もないとは言えないけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot deny that Chiaki's excessive pampering partly caused him to become so unable to function without her. The English instead says that viewed differently there was no issue, erasing his recognition that her cure also intensified the dependency he is now struggling to outgrow.
findings.japanese:
…まぁ、あいつに甘やかされすぎて
そうなってしまった側面もないとは言えないけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, I might've relied on her too much, but if you look at it from a different angle, it doesn't seem like there's any issue.

findings.highlight: two to three texts a day
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜からは、２、３日ペースで、疎遠とも親密とも言えない距離を守ってのメールが届く。
findings.explanation: Setsuna sends a carefully distanced message once every two or three days. The English says she sends two or three messages every day, multiplying the contact frequency by roughly an order of magnitude and destroying the fragile interval Haruki is monitoring.
findings.japanese:
雪菜からは、２、３日ペースで、
疎遠とも親密とも言えない距離を守ってのメールが届く。
findings.todokanai: As for Setsuna, she'll send me two to three texts a day, and the texts she sends don't feel like we're very distant, but they don't suggest that we're very close either.

findings.highlight: The content of her texts is also unchanged, never talking about how estranged or intimate we are and using polite language inconsistently.
findings.evidenceJa:
内容も相変わらず、疎遠とも親密とも言えない、
丁寧語があったりなかったりの、揺れた文面のまま。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's messages themselves maintain a tone neither distant nor intimate, wavering in and out of polite language; the English says their content never discusses estrangement or intimacy.
findings.japanese:
内容も相変わらず、疎遠とも親密とも言えない、
丁寧語があったりなかったりの、揺れた文面のまま。
findings.todokanai: The content of her texts is also unchanged, never talking about how estranged or intimate we are and using polite language inconsistently.

findings.highlight: From you and another one of my closest friends
findings.evidenceJa: お前とは別の、大切な大切な友達に。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that he has already been protected enough by a very, very dear friend other than Takeya—Chiaki. The English says Takeya and another friend both protected him, adding Takeya to the immediate claim and weakening the pointed contrast that explains why Haruki dismisses Takeya's warning.
findings.japanese:
俺は十分守ってもらってるから大丈夫だよ。
お前とは別の、大切な大切な友達に。
findings.todokanai: I'm fine now, I've already received enough protection. From you and another one of my closest friends.

findings.highlight: the element of romance in the story gradually increases
findings.evidenceJa: 物語は徐々に伝奇色を強めていき
findings.explanation: The story increasingly takes on the color of 伝奇: occult, supernatural legend and mystery, as the inhuman murders, demon bloodline, and heroine's identity emerge. The English calls this an increasing element of romance, misidentifying the genre movement that organizes the play and its source allusion.
findings.japanese:
そして物語は徐々に伝奇色を強めていき、
やがて意外な犯人像と、
意外な彼女の正体についても描かれる。
findings.todokanai: And the element of romance in the story gradually increases as the unexpected murderer is revealed along with the surprising twist of the girl's true identity.

findings.evidenceJa: セーラー服にショートカットの、言葉遣いと行動が乱暴な少女
findings.explanation: The second heroine is a rough-spoken, rough-acting girl in a sailor uniform with short-cropped hair. The English attaches 'shortcut' to the uniform, producing a nonexistent garment and omitting the visible hairstyle that helps distinguish Chiaki's second transformation.
findings.japanese:
第二部では主人公が交代し、
セーラー服にショートカットの、
言葉遣いと行動が乱暴な少女が舞台に現れた。
findings.todokanai: The main character changed for the second act, and a brazen girl in words and mannerisms wearing a shortcut sailor uniform appeared on the stage.

findings.highlight: the younger cousin had a quarrel with someone
findings.evidenceJa: 喧嘩相手でもある従兄の青年の夢を辿り、犯人の居場所を突き止めていく
findings.explanation: The heroine follows the dreams of her male cousin—who is also her habitual quarrel partner—to locate the culprit. The English says the cousin quarreled with some third party, changing the central pair's relationship and obscuring whose investigation the suspense plot follows.
findings.japanese:
喧嘩相手でもある従兄の青年の夢を辿り、
犯人の居場所を突き止めていくサスペンスストーリー。
findings.todokanai: This is a suspense story describing how the younger cousin had a quarrel with someone, and through his dreams, arrived at the culprit's whereabouts.

findings.highlight: I don't even mind if I have to stay at home all the time
findings.evidenceJa: だから本当は、ずっとこの家にいてくれたらいいなって、そう思う
findings.explanation: The fourth heroine tells her brother that being with him is fun and privately wishes he would stay in this house forever. The English says she herself does not mind having to stay home, reversing the person whose continued presence she desires.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、お兄ちゃんといるとすごく楽しいんだ。
だから本当は、ずっとこの家にいてくれたらいいなって、
そう思う」
findings.todokanai: "I'm happy as long as I can be with you, onii-chan. To tell you the truth, I don't even mind if I have to stay at home all the time."

findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の間取りや、流し台が、今までのセットより少し大きめに作ってある。
findings.explanation: The room layout and kitchen sink are built slightly larger than in the previous sets. The English turns the sink into a pond, making nonsense of the domestic interior and concealing the deliberate scale manipulation explained in the next line.
findings.japanese:
例えばこの四女の舞台…
部屋の間取りや、流し台が、
今までのセットより少し大きめに作ってある。
findings.todokanai: For example, during her act for the youngest daughter… The room and the pond's size seem slightly bigger than before.

findings.highlight: make the youngest heroine seem more natural
findings.evidenceJa: 四女の華奢さを際だたせるための、演出の妙。
findings.explanation: The oversized domestic set is a piece of stagecraft designed to accentuate the fourth heroine's slight, delicate build. The English says it makes her seem 'more natural' and merely makes the play interesting, removing the exact visual illusion Haruki is admiring.
findings.japanese:
それはきっと、第四の主人公である
四女の華奢さを際だたせるための、演出の妙。
findings.todokanai: All that to make the youngest heroine seem more natural, the way they set the stage is also part of the reason why the play is so interesting.

findings.highlight: even louder and longer than the cheers after our performance
findings.evidenceJa: その大きさと長さは、俺たちの演奏が終わったときの、雪菜とかずさに向けられた声援にだって引けを取ってない。
findings.explanation: The applause is no less loud or long than the cheers Setsuna and Kazusa received after the trio's performance. The English says it is even louder and longer, turning parity—the astonishing claim Haruki makes—into superiority.
findings.japanese:
その大きさと長さは、俺たちの演奏が終わったときの、
雪菜とかずさに向けられた声援にだって引けを取ってない。
findings.todokanai: It's even louder and longer than the cheers after our performance, it's just like the cheer Setsuna and Kazusa received.
